name: Spital-Land
agent: Declan Pollard, Sherry FitzGerald Pollard Fitzgerald, Clonmel
questions: What is the site area? From the photos and satellite we estimate about 0.08–0.12 ha (0.2–0.3 ac), mostly a walled gravel yard. Does any garden or land go with the house beyond the walls, and is the field behind available?
What is the yard across the R665, with the large shed, machinery and stockpiles? Is it a working business, and what are its hours and traffic?
Is the house on the public sewer, or a septic tank? The listing says only 'mains services connected'.
When was the house built, how are the walls built (cavity or block), and has any insulation been added? The BER is G at 440.95 kWh/m²/yr. How old are the oil boiler and the windows?
BuyerIQ flags the Eircode as in an EPA High Radon Area. Has a radon test been done, and has the house ever flooded? The Suir is about 400 m south.

ai.why: €290k plus a rough €75–130k retrofit comes to about €365–420k for a 186 m² dormer with a ground-floor bedroom beside a full bathroom, a 10-minute walk from Ardfinnan and 18 minutes from Clonmel's ED. Even finished, it stays a plain house on a small walled gravel plot right on the R665, with a commercial-looking yard across the road and no land for the dogs.

electricity.detail: Connected; the listing says 'Mains services connected'.

water.detail: Mains water, per the listing's 'mains services connected'.

sewer.detail: Likely the public sewer: the listing says 'mains services', and the house is inside Ardfinnan's built-up edge, but it doesn't name the sewer. Confirm it isn't a septic tank.

internet.detail: Full fibre at the address per BuyerIQ ('Fast broadband — 103 Mb full fibre'); the listing doesn't mention broadband, and the provider isn't confirmed.

groundFloorBedroom.detail: The floor plan shows Bedroom 1 (4.32 × 2.96 m, 12.8 m²) on the ground floor, next to the full bathroom with a bath (2.81 × 3.64 m). The second living room next to it (4.32 × 3.45 m) could become a fourth bedroom.

bedsNote: One double on the ground floor and two large doubles upstairs (4.82 × 3.99 m and 3.63 × 3.99 m, under the eaves with roof windows), plus a 2.34 × 3.23 m study. The 4.32 × 3.45 m second living room beside Bedroom 1 could become a fourth bedroom.
heating: Oil-fired central heating, with a stove in the sitting room and another in the second living room
tagline: A 186 m² three-bed dormer bungalow with a ground-floor bedroom and conservatory, BER G and in need of a full energy retrofit, on a small walled plot on the R665 at the north-east edge of Ardfinnan.

pros.text: €290k, with room for a full retrofit
pros.detail: About €1,560/m²; stamp duty €2,900. With a rough €75–130k of work the total comes to about €365–420k, well under €500k.

pros.text: Ground-floor bedroom beside a full bathroom
pros.detail: Bedroom 1 (12.8 m²) sits next to the 2.81 × 3.64 m bathroom with a bath. The 14.9 m² second living room beside it could become a second ground-floor bedroom, making a parents' wing.

About 0.8 km (10 min) on foot to the village centre and castle, and 0.94 km to Ardfinnan NS by OSM routing. Satellite suggests a footpath along the R665 the whole way, but Street View isn't checked yet.
Tipperary University Hospital, Clonmel (all ages, 24 h) is about 15.5 km. Cahir, with shops and secondary schools, is about 9 km away.
Sitting room (3.60 × 5.16 m), a second living room, a 4.03 × 4.35 m conservatory, a dining room and a study. The rooms add up to about 180 m².
BuyerIQ shows 103 Mb full fibre for E91 T186.

cons.text: Needs a deep energy retrofit, roughly €75–130k
cons.detail: Rough estimate. BER G at 441 kWh/m²/yr on oil. Walls, roof slopes and attic, windows and doors, and a heat pump come to €70–110k before about €25–35k of SEAI grants. Add €15–25k for an upstairs en-suite and bathroom upgrade and €15–30k to rework the galley kitchen. Expect months of disruption.

cons.text: Small walled gravel plot, no land for dogs
cons.detail: No plot size is stated. From the photos and satellite we estimate 0.08–0.12 ha (0.2–0.3 ac). Nearly all of it is gravel and tarmac yard inside block walls, with no lawn to speak of. The field behind isn't part of the sale as far as the listing says.

cons.text: On the R665, with a yard opposite
cons.detail: The house sits a few metres back from the R665 Clonmel road behind the yard wall. Across the road, about 40 m away, satellite shows a compound with a large shed, machinery and stockpiles, and a sand arena. Its use is unknown.

A 1990s–2000s style dormer with a pillared porch, a PVC conservatory and tidy but dated interiors. It isn't by the Suir (about 400 m south) or the castle, and there are neighbours about 15–25 m away on the road side.

cons.text: Only two bathrooms; small upstairs shower room
cons.detail: The upstairs shower room is 3.25 × 1.11 m and serves both upstairs bedrooms. The 2.37 m² store next to it could make an en-suite.

cons.text: Galley kitchen is narrow for six
cons.detail: The kitchen is 2.36 × 5.26 m (12.4 m²) and the dining room 2.46 × 3.83 m. Opening them up is part of the renovation estimate.

Cahir station (9 km) has only a few trains a day to Limerick Junction and Waterford, per Wikipedia. Direct Dublin trains run about hourly from Limerick Junction, roughly 35 km and 35 min away, taking about 1h30–1h45. Thurles is the alternative, about 48 km away.
BuyerIQ marks the Eircode as in an EPA High Radon Area and shows a second, hidden critical finding. It also lists 10 planning applications within 1 km, one of them an active build.
